futures.title: Futures
futures.lead: Binance USDT-M perpetuals and quarterlies: mark and index price, funding, open interest, positioning and live liquidations. All public, no key.
futures.liqHint: Binance's public stream, every pair. Totals accumulate while the tab is open.
futures.gl.mark.d: The contract's "fair" price, used by the exchange for unrealised PnL and liquidations. Derived from the index plus a smoothed funding premium, so a momentary spike in the order book can't liquidate you.
futures.gl.index.d: A volume-weighted average of the spot price across several exchanges: what the asset is "really" worth. The mark price gravitates around it.
futures.gl.funding.d: A periodic payment (every 8h) between longs and shorts that keeps the perpetual close to spot. Positive funding: longs pay shorts (the market is leveraged long). Negative: the reverse. Quoted per period; annualised = ×3×365.
futures.gl.oi.d: The value of every contract still open. It rises when new money enters positions and falls when they close or get liquidated. Rising price with rising OI = a trend with conviction behind it.
futures.gl.basis.d: The gap between a dated contract and the index. A positive basis (contango), annualised, is what the market pays to finance longs until delivery; it converges to zero at expiry.
futures.gl.liquidation.d: The forced close of a leveraged position once margin no longer covers the loss. A long liquidation executes as a sell (pushing price down), a short one as a buy. In cascades they move the market.
futures.gl.longshort.d: Accounts: share of traders net long vs net short. Top traders: the same, weighted by position size of the largest accounts. Taker: aggressive buy volume vs sell volume over the last hour.
futures.source: Data: Binance Futures (USDT-M), public endpoints, no key · chart: TradingView Lightweight Charts
